notes: Revision of v000 for a complete fictional cohort, not reconstruction or estimation of excluded target results. External evidence was independently re-read from the captured full articles: PMC6435188 v2 Table 1 and Methods, and PMC6897412 v1 Table 4 and Statistical analysis. Kenyan Maasai comparator means: female/male BMI 22.5/21.0, TC 3.8/4.0 mmol/L and HDL 1.2/1.1 mmol/L, with TC SD .9/1.1 and HDL SD .3/.32. Comparator volunteers were recruited in 2005, age >=17, with illness/pregnancy exclusions, and complete-case/activity-monitor selection; these are not population-identical estimates for the requested context. Tanzania/Uganda Table 4 reports adjusted LDL differences +.23 and +.48 mmol/L and HDL differences -.06 and -.15 for overweight and obese versus normal BMI. Their operator is categorical multiple linear regression with stratum, age, sex and selected upstream covariates, not the requested age/sex-only continuous TC or HDL slope. No retrieved evidence identifies the requested adjusted TC-HDL residual correlation. Retain v000's explicitly assumed demographic mixture: independent 55% F and 25% town-linked, age 18+Gamma(2.2,9) rejected above 85; 75% rural-linked. Town is a latent diet/activity/access scenario, not an observed lifestyle variable. Conditional BMI mean is 20.8 plus 1.2 for F, 3.3 for town, .025 per age-year centered at38, shifted lognormal above12 with SD3.3/4.3. Reference BMI22, age38; reference lipid means3.8/1.15, with centered sex and town effects as specified. All proportions, continuous slopes, age/sex/town effects and law choices are assumptions on external plausible scales; LDL-category evidence does not establish a continuous TC slope. The latent correlation .35 is assumed, not a reported residual correlation, nor determined simply by HDL being part of TC. No parameter was tuned to a target or to a desired generated analysis. Mathematical correction: v000 exponentiated a positive multiple of unbounded lognormal BMI, giving TC infinite positive moments despite ordinary finite samples. Replace only its TC BMI link by 3.8+.055*(BMI-22), multiplied by the original bounded age/sex/town factor. This is >3.25 before multiplication and preserves reference value and local derivative, with finite polynomial moments. Negative-BMI-coefficient HDL mean is bounded above and unchanged. Independent-of-predictors bivariate mean-one lognormal residual errors, CVs .22/.28 and latent correlation .35, are unchanged. All required first/second and mixed moments are now finite mathematically; finite samples alone do not prove this. Strict positivity uses construction, with an explicit numerical validity check that raises rather than excludes rows. No TC>HDL constraint, clipping or row-removal rule is applied. Exact six requested columns and 3000 rows; no actual participants, missingness, clustering, pregnancy/treatment/HIV or assay-batch strata are modeled. Target transportability and source/parameter uncertainty remain unmodeled. Local link coefficients do not equal the exact requested adjusted OLS slopes because latent-town mixing, nonlinear HDL and multiplicative effects affect them. Run generate(None,spec,seed) for data; analysis regresses each lipid on intercept, age, F and BMI, converts the BMI coefficient by 5*38.67 for mg/dL per 5 kg/m^2, and correlates lipid residuals. Synthetic sampling variability is not target-population uncertainty.
